summary.headline: Brigade Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 38% (vs 26%) on INR1,250 Cr revenue; presales of ~INR2,900 Cr in H1 vs INR9,000 Cr full-year guidance.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 saw the launch cycle return, with 2.4 mn sq ft launched at ~INR3,000 Cr GDV, and net sales of INR1,827 Cr on 1.32 mn sq ft (up 72% QoQ in value, 78% QoQ in area). Presales fell 10% YoY, which management attributed to launch timing, while average realisation rose 29% YoY to INR13,841/sq ft. Consolidated revenue was INR1,250 Cr and EBITDA INR478 Cr (38% margin vs 26%), led by Real Estate margin of 24% (vs 12%). Collections fell to INR1,633 Cr, partly due to a ~INR250-260 Cr milestone billed in September that remained uncollected, and operating cash flow was INR246 Cr. Management reiterated the INR9,000 Cr presales guidance and expects H2 to contribute ~INR7,000 Cr.

segments.name: Real Estate (residential)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR760 Cr, EBITDA INR178 Cr at 24% margin. Q2 residential sales of INR1,700 Cr: Bengaluru and Mysuru ~INR900 Cr, Hyderabad ~INR580 Cr, Chennai ~INR225 Cr. Two-thirds of volume came from sustenance sales.

segments.name: Leasing (commercial + FM)
segments.commentary: Operating leasing area 9.6 mn sq ft at 90% occupancy after adding Brigade Square Trivandrum (185,000 sq ft, 100% pre-leased) and Arcadia. Segment revenue INR329 Cr with EBITDA INR242 Cr (73%). Aureya FM manages 16 mn sq ft, revenue INR71 Cr, EBITDA margin 30%.

segments.name: Hospitality (BHVL)
segments.commentary: Portfolio ARR INR7,876 (+11% YoY), RevPAR INR5,922 (+10% YoY) at 75% occupancy; Bengaluru occupancy 81%, RevPAR +12%. Growth described as rate-led.

guidance_outlook: Full-year residential presales guidance reiterated at INR9,000 Cr; H1 presales ~INR2,888-2,900 Cr implies ~INR7,000 Cr in H2.

Launch pipeline for H2: 7 mn sq ft / INR7,600 Cr GDV. Two large Bengaluru townships (~INR3,800 Cr combined GDV, Whitefield-Hoskote and North Bengaluru) targeted for Q3, with one possibly slipping to Q4; Chennai 1 mn sq ft (one project Jan 2027, other may slip to next FY); Hyderabad 1 mn sq ft in Q4.
FY27 residential revenue recognition ~INR5,000 Cr (rough order of magnitude), with full-year YoY growth; Real Estate EBITDA margin guided at 22-24% for FY27.
Operating cash flow for FY27 expected higher than FY26; H1 operating cash generation ~INR600 Cr with H2 expected to be much higher.
Net debt-to-equity expected to rise from 0.31x to between 0.4x and 0.5x by end-March 2027, but stay under 0.5x.
Office rental income expected at ~INR1,700 Cr in FY29; operational leasing area to grow from 8.2 mn sq ft (office) to 12.4 mn sq ft by FY29 (9.5-12.5 mn sq ft total range quoted).
Office capex balance ~INR3,350 Cr: ~INR400 Cr in H2 FY27, ~INR1,500 Cr in FY28 and ~INR1,500 Cr in FY29.
capex_capacity: Commercial development under construction: 6.8 mn sq ft, including WTC Hyderabad and Orion Mall Hyderabad; WTC Hyderabad, Brigade Industrial Park Block 1 (~300,000 sq ft) and Brigade Icon commercial tower (~410,000 sq ft) slated to open by FY30; Orion Mall ~1.72 mn sq ft.

Land: ~12.5-13 mn sq ft added in H1 FY27, of which ~10 mn sq ft in Q2, ~INR13,000 Cr GDV; land additions mainly West and East Bengaluru, plus Hyderabad and Chennai. Q2 land payments ~INR440 Cr, split roughly equally between Bengaluru and Hyderabad.
Balance land payable ~INR2,000-2,300 Cr, mostly over the next year, with some timing deferral possible under joint development milestones.
Lease-up priorities: WTC Bengaluru and Brigade Twin Towers. Re-leasing at ~15% above prior rent; standard 5% annual escalation.
Ongoing supply to be phased in line with occupier demand.
demand_pricing: Launches in Q2: Brigade Barcelona (Neopolis, Hyderabad) INR475 Cr launch-quarter sales; Misty Greens (Mysuru) almost fully sold, ~INR150 Cr; Azalea (Brigade Meadows, Bengaluru) senior-living project. Barcelona expected to add INR300-325 Cr more in H2, ~INR800 Cr for FY27; unit size ~INR4 Cr; absorption slower than Brigade Gateway Hyderabad.

Sustenance sales in H1 ~INR1,100 Cr-scale (about 80% of H1 sales); key contributors Brigade Eternia, Belvedere, Insignia (Bengaluru), Gateway (Hyderabad) and Icon (Chennai), plus Citadel-adjacent smaller projects. Management hopes to repeat H1 sustenance levels in H2.
Upcoming Bengaluru launches mostly priced INR1-2 Cr; North Bengaluru ~INR1-1.5 Cr; majority under INR3 Cr; ~20% of Bengaluru volume around INR3 Cr.
Average realisation INR13,841/sq ft, +29% YoY, from price increases and higher-end mix.
Management sees IT/AI job-related weakness as not yet impacting demand; demand described as shifting to premium.
Office demand: GCCs 41% of Q2 leasing; green-certified tech parks 61% of absorption. Rental collections 99%.

qa_highlights.question: Sucrit Patil: what is residential volume guidance for next quarters, execution risk on 2.4 mn sq ft launches, and margin strategy against input cost spikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Presales guidance of INR9,000 Cr reiterated; H1 presales ~INR2,888-2,900 Cr, leaving ~INR7,000 Cr for H2 from Q3/Q4 launches. Management said execution risk on launches is not material; the main gating item is approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Sucrit Patil: FY27/FY28 capex and debt guidance, and working capital and liquidity management across leasing and hospitality?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 operating cash generation ~INR600 Cr, with H2 much higher on September milestone collections and sales-led collections. Net debt-to-equity to rise from 0.31x to 0.4-0.5x by end-March, staying under 0.5x; capex funded by a mix of internal accruals and debt.

qa_highlights.question: Biplab Debbarma: how will Bengaluru residential demand evolve given IT/AI job losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IT hiring weakness has not hit demand; demand has shifted to premium, with GCC absorption of talent. Indications for upcoming launches are good, but it will be tested only at approval and launch.

qa_highlights.question: Biplab Debbarma: GDV and timing of Q3 launches, and rental income growth into FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Two large Bengaluru townships total ~INR3,800 Cr GDV; one targeted Q3, the other Q3 or slipping to Q4. Office portfolio to rise from 8.2 mn sq ft to 12.4 mn sq ft by FY29 (9.5-12.5 mn sq ft range); rental income ~INR1,700 Cr in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Jimeet Shah: vacancy and exit rentals at WTC Bengaluru and Twin Towers, and whether H2 sales velocity will pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: About 100,000 sq ft leased at WTC Bengaluru and about 100,000 sq ft sold at Twin Towers in Q2; re-leasing at ~15% above prior rent with 5% annual escalation. H2 sales will rely more on launches, as 80% of H1 sales came from sustenance; Bengaluru launches priced INR1-2 Cr are expected to absorb well.

qa_highlights.question: Harsh Pathak: size of milestone shortfall in collections and the construction payables position?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR250-260 Cr of a September-billed milestone remained uncollected; trade receivables rose ~INR200 Cr. About INR90 Cr of construction payables was reinstated under Ind AS accounting, so the underlying construction outlay is ~INR800-810 Cr.

qa_highlights.question: Harsh Pathak: Barcelona sales ramp-up, sustenance run-rate and Hyderabad demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Barcelona did INR450-475 Cr in Q2; management expects another INR300-325 Cr in H2 (~INR800 Cr for FY27), unit size ~INR4 Cr. Absorption is slower than Brigade Gateway Hyderabad. Management hopes H2 sustenance matches H1 (~INR1,100 Cr).

qa_highlights.question: Pritesh Sheth: Chennai launch timing and the 7 mn sq ft city split; OCF and land addition details?
qa_highlights.answer: Chennai: one project likely January 2027; the other may slip to next FY. The 7 mn sq ft split is 1 mn each in Hyderabad and Chennai, rest in Bengaluru. Land additions focused on West and East Bengaluru, with some Hyderabad and Chennai.

qa_highlights.question: Parvez Qazi: Bengaluru ticket-size mix and office capex phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Most Bengaluru units are below INR1.5 Cr (North Bengaluru INR1-1.5 Cr), with the rest around INR2 Cr and ~20% near INR3 Cr. Office capex: ~INR400 Cr in H2 FY27, ~INR1,500 Cr in FY28 and ~INR1,500 Cr in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Parvez Qazi / Biplab Debbarma: office assets beyond FY29 and construction status?
qa_highlights.answer: WTC Hyderabad, Brigade Industrial Park Block 1 (~300,000 sq ft), Brigade Icon tower (~410,000 sq ft) and Orion Mall (1.72 mn sq ft) are under construction and slated for operations by FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Harsh Pathak: FY27 residential revenue recognition and margin; FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 residential revenue recognition ~INR5,000 Cr (rough order of magnitude), with full-year growth; Real Estate margin 22-24% for FY27, as in H1. FY28 not yet projected, depends on OC timing.

qa_highlights.question: Harsh Pathak: INR28 Cr PE payment and INR317 Cr equity-method investment?
qa_highlights.answer: INR28 Cr is distributions to a JV partner. The INR317 Cr equity-method balance relates to Vibrancy Real Estates, where Bain Capital invested in Q1 and the entity became a JV, so it was reclassified out of consolidation.

qa_highlights.question: Vasudev: Q2 business development and timing of the ~INR2,000-2,300 Cr balance land payable?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 land additions ~12.5-13 mn sq ft, of which ~10 mn sq ft in Q2, ~INR13,000 Cr GDV. Balance land payable is mostly over the next year, with some deferral possible under joint development milestones.

risks_watch: Launch timing slippage: one Bengaluru township may move from Q3 to Q4, and one Chennai project may move to FY28, which would put the H2 INR7,000 Cr presales ask at risk.
Barcelona absorption is slower than Brigade Gateway Hyderabad, and H2 velocity depends more on launches as sustenance (~80% of H1 sales) is expected to decline in share.
Collections: ~INR250-260 Cr September milestone uncollected; trade receivables up ~INR200 Cr; Q2 collections of INR1,633 Cr versus INR2,003 Cr in Q2 FY26.
Leverage rising from 0.31x to 0.4-0.5x by end-March 2027 as land (balance ~INR2,000-2,300 Cr) and office capex (~INR3,350 Cr) are funded; ~85% of debt is backed by rental and GOP cash flows.
Macro: 25 bps RBI repo hike noted; IT/AI job weakness may affect Bengaluru demand over 2-3 years; Chennai approval cycle after government change is a watch item.
Leasing: WTC Bengaluru and Brigade Twin Towers lease-up and sales remain priorities; no exit rentals or vacancy quantum were given.
key_quotes: For now, we reiterate the INR9,000 crores presales guidance.
While presales was 10% lower than Q2 FY26, this is mostly reflective of the launch timing this year and not of the demand on ground.
So the margin profile of the entire FY27 would -- in real estate would be in that early 20s, between 22% and 24%, which is what was there in H1 as well.
The reduction in collection number as compared to earlier quarters was primarily due to milestone that got billed in the third month of the quarter and for which collections were in progress.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, pricing and the FY27 presales and margin guidance, which were reiterated without change. More cautious and less specific on launch timing (Bengaluru township and Chennai may slip), FY28 revenue recognition (deferred pending OCs), Barcelona absorption pace, and the Q2 collections gap.
